answer: A place I go to be completely alone is a quiet stretch of the riverbank a short walk from my home, well beyond the busy part of the embankment where people gather in the evenings. To reach it, you follow a narrow path past a few fields and a clump of bamboo, and then the river suddenly opens up in front of you. I tend to go there once or twice a week, and more often whenever I feel overwhelmed and need to clear my head. It is a [[secluded]] spot that few people seem to know about, which is exactly why I love it. I usually just sit on the grass under an old tree, watch the water and let my thoughts settle. Occasionally I bring a book, but more often I do nothing at all, which I rarely get to do these days. There is something deeply [[restorative]] about being alone in nature, with no phone buzzing and no one demanding my attention. I go alone because at home and at work I am constantly surrounded by people, and although I love them, I also need time to [[recharge my batteries]]. I find that a bit of [[solitude]] helps me process my feelings and make sense of whatever is bothering me. Far from feeling lonely, I feel more like myself there than almost anywhere else. Honestly, in a world that never seems to stop, having a private place to simply be is [[a rare luxury]]. I always return home feeling calmer and more centred.

followUps.q: Do you think it is important to spend time alone?
followUps.answer: Yes, I do. Time alone gives you space to reflect and understand your own feelings. Without it, I think people can become stressed and lose touch with what really matters to them.

followUps.q: Does your family know about this place?
followUps.answer: My younger sister does, and she teases me about my secret hideout. My parents know I go for walks by the river, but I do not think they know exactly where I go.
